subject: Immunology
vignette: A 7-year-old boy is brought for progressive difficulty walking that began around age 3. Examination shows a wide-based ataxic gait, dysmetria, and involuntary choreoathetoid movements. Slit-lamp and direct examination of the eyes reveals conjunctival telangiectasias. He has had recurrent sinus infections and bronchitis. Serum shows markedly low IgA, low IgG2, and elevated alpha-fetoprotein. MRI shows cerebellar atrophy without mass lesion.
question: Which of the following is the most likely underlying genetic and cellular defect in this patient?

options.text: Mutations in the ATM gene causing defective DNA double-strand break repair and increased radiosensitivity
Deletion of 22q11.2 causing cardiac defects, hypocalcemia, and absent thymus
Mutation in WAS gene causing defective actin cytoskeleton reorganization in lymphocytes
Mutation in CYBB causing defective NADPH oxidase in phagocytes
Deficiency of adenosine deaminase causing accumulation of toxic purine metabolites in lymphocytes

explanation_correct: Ataxia-telangiectasia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in ATM, a kinase that orchestrates the DNA damage response to double-strand breaks. The phenotype combines progressive cerebellar ataxia beginning in early childhood, oculocutaneous telangiectasias, variable humoral and cellular immunodeficiency (especially low IgA, IgG2, and IgE), elevated alpha-fetoprotein, and a markedly increased risk of hematopoietic malignancies. Because DNA repair is faulty, patients are hypersensitive to ionizing radiation, whose use should be minimized in diagnostic and therapeutic settings.

explanation_incorrect.B: 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge syndrome) causes cardiac defects, hypocalcemia, and thymic hypoplasia but not progressive ataxia with telangiectasias or elevated alpha-fetoprotein.
explanation_incorrect.C: WAS mutation causes Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, characterized by microthrombocytopenia, eczema, and immunodeficiency rather than cerebellar degeneration.
explanation_incorrect.D: CYBB mutation causes chronic granulomatous disease, which presents with granulomatous infections and a defective respiratory burst.
explanation_incorrect.E: Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes a severe combined immunodeficiency with lymphopenia, presenting in infancy rather than ataxia at age 7.

educationalObjective: Ataxia-telangiectasia results from ATM mutations impairing DNA double-strand break repair, producing ataxia, telangiectasias, IgA deficiency, elevated AFP, and radiosensitivity.

subject: Immunology
vignette: An 11-year-old girl with known ataxia-telangiectasia has had recurrent sinopulmonary infections treated with antibiotics and immunoglobulin replacement. She now presents with a painless neck mass. Lymph node biopsy shows a B-cell lymphoma. Her parents ask whether she should receive chest radiotherapy as part of treatment and whether her siblings need testing.
question: Which of the following best describes the most important management consideration and risk associated with this disorder?

options.text: Radiotherapy is safe and recommended because DNA repair in this disorder affects only lymphocytes
Siblings need no testing because the disorder is X-linked
Radiation therapy should be minimized because ATM deficiency causes hypersensitivity and there is a high lifetime malignancy risk
Immunoglobulin replacement removes the need to monitor for malignancy
The main risk for this patient is anaphylaxis to blood products from IgA-containing plasma

explanation_correct: ATM deficiency impairs repair of DNA double-strand breaks in all tissues, so patients are radiosensitive and should receive ionizing radiation sparingly; they also have a markedly elevated lifetime risk of lymphoreticular malignancies (leukemia and lymphoma) and some solid tumors, even when immunoglobulin replacement controls infections. Ataxia-telangiectasia is autosomal recessive, so siblings have a 25% risk if both parents are carriers and merit genetic counseling and testing. Malignancy surveillance is a key part of long-term care.

explanation_incorrect.A: ATM is a ubiquitous DNA repair kinase; radiosensitivity affects all tissues, and radiation can cause severe toxicity in these patients.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ataxia-telangiectasia is autosomal recessive, so both male and female siblings may be affected and should be offered testing.
explanation_incorrect.D: Immunoglobulin replacement reduces infection burden but does not reduce the intrinsic malignancy risk from defective DNA repair.
explanation_incorrect.E: Anaphylaxis to IgA in blood products is a concern in selective IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibodies, not the central issue here.

educationalObjective: Ataxia-telangiectasia patients are radiosensitive and have a high lifetime malignancy risk, so radiation should be minimized and families counseled about autosomal recessive inheritance.
